content: Sambar is a South Indian stew made with lentils, mixed vegetables, tamarind broth, and a special spice blend called sambar powder.

Garam masala is a warm spice blend used extensively in Indian cooking. It often contains spices such as cumin, coriander, cardamom, cinnamon, and cloves. It is usually added toward the end of cooking to add aroma and warmth.
Rasam is a thin, spicy South Indian soup traditionally prepared using tamarind juice as a base, with the addition of tomato, chili pepper, pepper, cumin, and other spices.

Biryani is a mixed rice dish made with Indian spices, rice, and usually some type of meat or vegetables. Curd (yogurt) is often used in the marinade to tenderize the meat and add richness to the dish.
Tamarind can be substituted with a mix of lime juice (for sourness) and a little jaggery or sugar (for sweetness), or by using amchur (dry mango powder).
Curd (yogurt) can be substituted with sour cream, or buttermilk depending on the recipe.
Dosa is a thin batter-based dish originating from South India, made from a fermented batter consisting of lentils and rice.
To make soft chapatis, use warm water and a little oil or ghee when kneading the dough. Rest the dough for at least 15-20 minutes, and cook them on a hot tawa.
